summary: Dedicated capacity degradation during canary model rollout caused throttling, streaming stalls, and invoice delta for Peregrine Logistics
description:
Issue summary:
Peregrine Logistics experienced elevated 429 throttles, streaming disconnects, and an unexpected invoice delta on 2026-03-10 following a scheduled canary rollout of gptx-13b-quantized-v2 into their dedicated pool. Impact included partial request failures for interactive workflows and duplicated billed tokens for reconnects.

Impact:
- ~35% of Peregrine's requests returned transient 429 or aborted streaming during the 11:40–12:50 UTC window.
- Several long-running chat sessions observed partial token double-counting resulting in ~2.3% higher billed usage for the hour.
- Customer-visible outages affected order-tracking bot and ETA summaries (high business impact).

Timeline (UTC):
- 11:30: Canary rollout (5%) of gptx-13b-quantized-v2 started for Peregrine dedicated pool.
- 11:40: First alerts: increased 429s and streaming reconnects on dedicated nodes.
- 11:45: Customer reported degraded UX via #support Slack thread and Support portal.
- 11:55: Support escalated to SRE; mitigation: paused further canary expansion.
- 12:10: Engineering observed autoscaler churn and scheduling backpressure on a subset of GPU hosts.
- 12:25: Billing team flagged anomalous token meter spikes for same customer.
- 12:35: Rollback of canary to previous model.
- 12:50: Token metering patch deployed to stop duplicate counting; streaming reconnect rate dropped.
- 13:05: Full service restored for customer; credits/pilot invoice correction initiated.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Simulate canary-scale burst in dedicated pool with mixed short/long streaming sessions.
2. Force node pod preemption to trigger reconnects during open streaming sessions.
3. Verify metering increments for reconnect paths under simulated network flaps.

Relevant logs and dashboards:
- Serving runtime logs: /var/log/serving/runtime/pool-peregrine-03-10.log (query by trace_id)
- Scheduler alerts graph: /dashboards/scheduler/churn?from=2026-03-10T11:00Z&to=2026-03-10T13:00Z
- Billing metering exports: s3://billing-dumps/2026/03/10/peregrine-metering.csv

investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: Interplay between canary allocation (bursting new quantized kernels), scheduler autoscaler heuristics, and a pre-ack token metering path created a brief window where reconnects were counted twice.
Observations: Some GPU hosts experienced transient memory pressure when the quantized kernel warmed up, causing pod restarts and reconnect storms from clients pinned to those hosts.
Metering bug: token-counter increment happened on connect and on reconnect confirm, resulting in duplicate rows when a session re-established within a short window.
Mitigations validated: Rolling back to prior model removed the kernel warmup pressure; metering hotfix prevented further double-counting; scheduler circuit-breaker reduced autoscaler churn.
resolution_notes: Immediate actions: Rolled back canary, paused scheduled canaries for dedicated customers for 48h, deployed a metering hotfix (PR #1923) to dedupe token increments on reconnect, scaled up dedicated capacity by 10% temporarily to absorb backlog.
Customer remediation: Issued invoice credit covering the duplicated token delta; CS provided a one-week free dedicated buffer as goodwill (documented in customer account).

Longer-term fixes: Add pre-warm checks for quantized kernels, implement model rollout pacing with health checks for dedicated pools, and adjust autoscaler thresholds to be more conservative during canary phases.
